messages:
maria: Heads-up — getting a p95/p99 regression report from support for tenant `acme-corp` after last runtime rollout (v2.3.1). SLOs show p95 ~+40ms and p99 ~+220ms on chat/generate routes since 07:22 UTC.

kyle: ack. link to dashboard?

maria: https://grafana.redwood.local/d/ABCD/runtime-latency?orgId=1&from=now-1h&to=now — look at route=/v1/generate (seq > 512). Spike aligns with 07:18 deploy window.

rahul: seeing it in traces too, tails are wide. Sampling 100 p99 traces now. initial signal: host-level qdepth spikes + longer kernel time on a subset of pods.

olivia: any auth 429s or 503s mixed in? might be backpressure.

support-jen: support ticket #9872, tenant reports timeouts for some long-context prompts (chatbot flows). They sent curl reproducer and avg latency numbers. No increased error rate, mostly latency.

maria: deploy-bot reports rollout: runtime:v2.3.1 with kernel-selector tweak and batching heuristic change (auto-batch threshold lowered).

deploy-bot: [deploy] runtime:v2.3.1 started 2026-03-12T07:15Z -> 20% -> 50% -> 100% (completed 07:19Z).

kyle: interesting — kernel selector change could pick a slower kernel for long sequences on some GPUs. rahul, any correlation by kernel type?

rahul: quick grep of traces: about 62% of p99 traces used `kernel-v3` vs 9% baseline. median per-token kernel time ~ +15%. pushing a query for cohort split by model, seq_len, and kernel id. query: 
```
select kernel_id, model, count(*) as n, p95(latency_ms) from traces
where route='/v1/generate' and seq_len>512 and ts>now()-1h
group by kernel_id, model
```

rahul: result (sample): kernel-v3 / model-x-large / n=423 / p99=1240ms; kernel-v2 / model-x-large / n=58 / p99=980ms. So v3 is higher but not uniformly.

olivia: could be dataset-dependent cache effects (KV cache layout) — kernel-v3 might be using a different attention kernel that interacts poorly with our KV cache sharding on some hosts.

maria: action plan proposals: 1) rollback runtime to v2.3.0 for affected tenant cohort; 2) bisect kernel selector config (force kernel-v2 on a small cohort) to confirm; 3) add temporary routing rule to prefer warm KV hosts for long-seq traffic; 4) notify support + customer. Which first?

kyle: let's bisect quickly by routing 5% traffic to a cohort pinned to v2.3.0 and 5% to v2.3.1 but force kernel-v2 to isolate selector. If kernel pin brings p99 down, we know selector is culprit.

rahul: I'll spin up an experiment: create two cohorts — cohort-A (v2.3.0) and cohort-B (v2.3.1 + kernel=force-v2). Load test with sampled traffic from support reproducer.

support-jen: can provide a masked reproducer and sample payloads. I'll attach ticket artifacts.

olivia: also add a temporary throttling rule (<200 concurrent long-seq requests per host) to reduce queuing while we triage. That should help tail while we test.

maria: rahul, rough runbook steps for the experiment so we can do it quickly:
- create routing cohort config: `route_rule { tenant: "acme-corp-test" -> runtime_version: "v2.3.0" }` and another with `kernel_override: "v2"`
- start traffic replay at low rate (2rps -> 20rps) and watch p95/p99, qdepth, kernel-time histograms
- collect 200 p99 traces per cohort

rahul: doing it now. will post short diff metrics.

(10m passes)

rahul: experiment results: cohort-A(v2.3.0) p99=980ms, cohort-B(v2.3.1+kernelforce-v2) p99=990ms, production v2.3.1 (no override) p99=1240ms. Looks like forcing kernel-v2 brings p99 down close to v2.3.0.

olivia: that strongly implicates kernel-selector picking kernel-v3 under certain scheduling/host conditions. Good repro.

maria: ok rollout mitigation: 1) immediate routing patch to bias long-seq requests away from hosts that picked kernel-v3 (if we can identify via host labels) OR 2) rollback runtime to v2.3.0 while we fix selector. Which is lower risk?

kyle: rollback is safest for customer impact but costs time. We can do targeted routing first to reduce blast radius and buy time. Also add kernel selector kill-switch that prefers kernel-v2 globally for long-seq until we root cause.

maria: agree. rahul, prepare PR for route rule + selector kill-switch. set support comms. olivia, throttle rule?

rahul: PR opened: https://git.redwood/repo/routing/PR/512 — includes 3 changes: 1) route bias for seq_len>512 to hosts label `kernel-prefer=v2` (5% -> 50%), 2) global selector flag `KERNEL_OVERRIDE=v2` (off by default), 3) instrumentation to log kernel_id on perf traces.

olivia: throttle rule ticket #221 opened, will apply soft limit 200 conc long-seq on prod tier in next 5m.

support-jen: I told acme-corp we're triaging and applying mitigations; asked for permission to add them to a short A/B test. They replied OK.

maria: timeline: apply route bias (5%) now, monitor 10m; if p99 drop >20% for acme cohort, increase to 50%; otherwise rollback.

(12m)

rahul: route bias 5% applied. initial metrics: acme p99 down 18% after 6m, qdepth down ~25% on biased hosts.

maria: good. increase to 50% and enable kernel override flag ramp to 10% for safety.

rahul: ramped. monitoring.

(8m)

rahul: after ramp, acme p99 stabilized at -35% from baseline. overall cluster p99 reduced too. No increased errors.

maria: support comms: notifying customer that we applied temporary routing + kernel override; longer-term fix: revert kernel-selector heuristic and add a server-side test to validate kernel perf on a wider sample of GPUs and seq lengths.

olivia: filing follow-up: reproduce on internal perf lab with 100 concurrent long-seq sessions across GPU matrix (A100, H100) and confirm memory pressure / kernel scheduling interplay.

kyle: once rollback/selector fix is ready we'll schedule a canary with expanded metrics and per-kernel perf baselines.

support-jen: customer confirmed improved latency on their side. Closing ticket pending longer-term patch.

maria: summary notes to paste into postmortem: cause=kernel-selector change in runtime:v2.3.1 that biased some hosts towards kernel-v3 for long sequences; root effect=per-token kernel time increase + queuing; mitigations=targeted routing bias + kernel override flag + throttle; next steps=fix selector heuristic, run GPU matrix perf tests, add per-kernel baselines to deploy gate.

kyle: I'll own the postmortem write-up. rahul/olivia will own follow-ups. Thanks team :thumbsup:
